description: SideBar — the navigation rail. A surface column on the canvas (the classic chrome split, both schemes) with a thick subtle inline-end border — the top bar's underline, rotated. Items stack with no gap (their underlines are the rhythm) in a true SLOT: designers add as many as they want. The Collapse item pins to the bottom. Expanded width 256 (authored, constant across densities); collapsed width DERIVES from the item's square edge (40/52/60) — so the rail is exactly as wide as its squares are tall. The collapsed submenu is the floating Menu: composition, not new anatomy. NOTE — collapsing an instance with edited items: slot content is the instance's own (that's the point of slots), so it does not follow the rail's Collapsed automatically. Multi-select the items and flip their Collapsed with the rail's; sub-items simply leave (their submenu floats). Fresh instances mirror automatically. In code this cascades: one data-collapsed on the nav.
notes: v0.2.0 (2026-09-05, Victor's sidebar review; v0.1.0 was a sketch of Menu-item instances). The items area is a real SLOT (Slots GA'd June 2026 — probe-verified in this file) seeded with three representative items. The accordion open-state is an interaction fact, recorded not built (polish). Seeded and instanced items MIRROR the rail's Collapsed axis (the builder matches shared variant axes by name). v0.3.0 (2026-09-05): the seed shows the OPEN submenu — Gas (selected) and Fields under Edit, labels aligned by the derived indent. Sub-items cannot mirror the Collapsed axis (they have none — a collapsed sidebar's submenu is the floating Menu), so the builder HIDES seeded instances that cannot follow a non-default axis value: collapse the rail and the sub-items leave, as the design says. v0.4.0 (2026-09-06, Victor): the Collapse control's icon flip is BUILT — collapsedOverrides on the collapse instance swap first_page for last_page (key 8d2cf7772cf7eb6efea11b909e8142ec3ec96396) in Collapsed variants; CSS carries the same flip as a mirror (scale: -1 1 on the pinned item's icon under data-collapsed), because the two glyphs are horizontal mirror twins: one svg in consumer markup, both directions.
